offence_severity: Minimum 6 months to maximum 10 years imprisonment
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation and planning to fabricate false evidence
motive: To shield accused no.1 from prosecution in the disproportionate assets case
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the accused fabricated false sale deeds and agreements to shield the appellant from prosecution in the disproportionate assets case.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the accused's defense of an escrow arrangement was raised belatedly and lacked credibility due to the delay and illegal stamp paper used.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 4.01.2001; Trial judgment: 06.01.2020; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: March 12, 2021
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Basva Prabhu Patil, Sr. Adv., Amit Anand Tiwari, Ms. Shakun Sharma, Kushagr Pandey, Ms. Devyani Gupta, B. Karunakaran, Anoop Prakash Awasthi, S. Gowthaman, Advs. Counsel for the State: Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, ASG., Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advs.
investigation_status: Case registered against the appellant under Section 120B read with Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the PC Act; search conducted at the appellant’s residence on 24.01.2001; investigation initiated under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(e), PC Act
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted; High Court: Confirmed trial court’s finding; Supreme Court: Dismissed appeals
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused fabricated false evidence during the investigation stage to shield the appellant from legal action in the disproportionate assets case, and that the investigating agency was entitled to register a case under Section 193, IPC.
defence_argument: The accused contended that the requirements of Section 195(1)(b)(i) and Section 340, Cr.P.C. were not complied with prior to framing the charge under Section 193, IPC, and that the investigation stage did not constitute a proceeding in any court for the purpose of Section 195(1)(b)(i), Cr.P.C.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the words 'in relation to' under Section 195(1)(b)(i), Cr.P.C. must be interpreted with a reasonably close nexus to the court proceedings, and that the investigation stage, while a stage of a judicial proceeding, does not equate to a proceeding in any court under Section 195(1)(b)(i), Cr.P.C.
precedent_relied_upon: Sachida Nand Singh and Another v. State of Bihar and Another, (1998) 2 SCC 493; Patel Laljibhai Somabhai AIR 1971 SC 1935; Iqbal Singh Marwah and Another v. Meenakshi Marwah and Another, (2005) 4 SCC 370
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the gravity of the offence, the elaborate conspiracy to fabricate false evidence, and the attempt to shield the appellant from prosecution, despite the High Court's leniency in reducing the sentences.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The High Court considered the advanced age of the accused and the delay in completion of the trial as mitigating factors.
other_sentence_order: The Appellants are directed to surrender for serving out the rest of their sentence, and the Registry is directed to release any fine deposited before the Court.
